title: Your providers. One place.
description: Bring the services you already use into one view. Browse your media across connected accounts and see what has changed.
highlights: A combined view
Find titles across your connected provider accounts without opening every service.
Pick up where you left off
See unfinished playback alongside the providers that hold your progress.
Follow your activity
Keep recent syncs and newly added titles close to the rest of your media.

title: Set it up. Let it sync.
description: Choose your provider pairs and the features you want to share. CrossWatch applies your configured rules on a recurring schedule.
highlights: Choose what moves
Select history, watchlists, ratings and other supported features for each pair.
Choose the rhythm
Run hourly, daily or at a custom interval that suits your setup.
Keep track of results
Use the dashboard and activity views to see how each run went.

title: See the changes. Make the call.
description: Review a proposed sync before applying it. Inspect additions, updates and removals, correct matches, and choose which changes to keep.
highlights: Understand the plan
See what CrossWatch proposes for the source and destination.
Correct the match
Resolve title and episode mappings before the selected changes are applied.
Stay in control
Select the changes you want and leave the rest out of that run.

title: Make the steps work together.
description: Go beyond a recurring sync. Build a plan around the order of your pairs, scheduled captures and playback activity.
highlights: Run in sequence
Arrange pair runs and start a step after another one finishes.
Capture on a schedule
Create provider restore points at the times and on the days you choose.
React to activity
Trigger a sync pair from Watcher or webhook events.

title: A tracker you can call your own.
description: Keep your media history on your own server. Browse your watches, ratings and progress in CrossWatch, and bring in activity from connected services.
highlights: Your record of what you watch
Browse movies and episodes and keep your viewing history together.
Keep the details
Add watches, keep notes and correct records when needed.
Connected to your setup
Import activity and use the local tracker alongside your other providers.

title: Keep a way back.
description: Protect the CrossWatch setup you have built. Back up selected configuration and data, then recover the parts you need.
highlights: Save your setup
Include configuration, mappings, blocks, selected local trackers and captures.
Keep another copy
Store an optional encrypted copy through WebDAV, Nextcloud or a mounted folder.
Recover what matters
Restore selected data or recover a tracker into a new instance.

title: A point in time. Ready to revisit.
description: Save a provider dataset at a moment you choose. Browse captures, compare changes over time and restore captured data to a provider profile.
highlights: Choose the scope
Capture watchlists, ratings, history or progress for a provider profile.
See what changed
Compare two captures to inspect added, removed and updated records.
Make it routine
Schedule captures and manage their retention alongside your setup.

title: Get the right titles together.
description: Make the data behind your sync easier to understand. Inspect records, correct matches and handle different episode numbering.
highlights: Inspect the records
Browse provider data, title IDs, watch dates, ratings and progress.
Save the right match
Correct mismatched titles and reuse your mappings in future syncs.
Handle episode differences
Map split or combined episodes and manage the items you want to block.

title: Playback happens. Tracking follows.
description: Send playback activity from your media servers and supported clients to your chosen trackers, with separate routes for different users.
highlights: Connect your routes
Choose a playback source and the destinations that should receive its activity.
Keep people separate
Route each user to their own tracker accounts.
Ready for everyday watching
Watcher works without Plex Pass or Emby Premiere.

title: One installation. Everyone included.
description: Give each person a place in CrossWatch while keeping their accounts and activity separate.
highlights: A setup for each person
Scope provider connections and sync pairs to the right profile.
Their routes and routines
Keep Watcher routes and schedules aligned with each user.
Shared installation
Manage your household in one place with optional user logins.

title: Put your lists to work.
description: Connect lists across services and publish them for the tools in your media setup.
highlights: Connect your lists
Map a source list to a destination and choose its synchronization behavior.
Keep collections useful
Bring provider list management into the same setup as your other sync tasks.
Publish for your tools
Use published lists with tools such as Kometa, Radarr and Sonarr.

title: See what happened across your setup.
description: Follow your media activity from individual titles to complete sync runs, with results for each destination.
highlights: Start with a title
Explore the activity associated with a movie or episode.
Inspect the run
See which provider pairs participated and what changed.
Keep the context
Follow watching, ratings, captures and backups alongside sync results.

title: The details, when you need them.
description: Read the raw logs behind CrossWatch activity and share useful diagnostics when investigating an issue.
highlights: Find the right run
Browse saved sessions and filter the output you need.
Read the raw output
Inspect diagnostic messages with their run context.
Share the evidence
Copy or download logs to include with an issue report.

title: Understand the differences.
description: Explore saved sync data to find missing records, mismatches and items waiting for another attempt.
highlights: Compare both sides
See records found in one saved snapshot but not confirmed in the other.
Investigate an item
Inspect its IDs, matching information and the reason it needs attention.
Prepare a correction
Use mapping and blocking tools to improve a future run.

title: See how your services connect.
description: Take a wider view of your sync routes and understand how data moves through your setup.
highlights: Follow the connections
Visualize the enabled routes between your provider accounts.
Understand the flow
See how one-way and two-way pairs fit together.
Refine your setup
Identify overlapping routes and loops as your provider network grows.

title: Keep the watches outside your server, too.
description: Log activity that happened elsewhere and send it to the providers you choose.
highlights: Find the title
Look up the movie or show you want to add activity for.
Choose the activity
Record a watch, a rating or a watchlist action.
Choose the destinations
Send the action to one or more of your connected providers.

title: Ask about your own setup.
description: Bring your own AI model to CrossWatch for help understanding your installation, or connect an AI app with read-only access.
highlights: Ask in CrossWatch
Use the built-in assistant to explore questions about your setup.
Bring your own model
Configure the AI connection you want to use.
Use your preferred app
Connect tools such as Claude, Codex or Cursor through read-only MCP access.

title: Make CrossWatch your own.
description: Bring the hub online, connect your first services and build your setup a little at a time.
highlights: Start the container
Run CrossWatch with persistent storage for its configuration and data.
Connect your services
Add your accounts and metadata, then configure a first provider pair.
See it working
Try a dry run or Interactive Sync, inspect the result and add your schedule.

title: A home on your own server.
description: Run CrossWatch in a container with its web interface, sync engine and local data together.
highlights: Save the configuration
Use the Compose example on this page as your starting point.
Keep your data
Mount persistent storage at /config so settings and local data survive container updates.
Open CrossWatch
Start the container, open the web interface and connect your services.

title: CrossWatch on your Unraid server.
description: Add CrossWatch to the server you already use for your media and manage it alongside your other containers.
highlights: Install from Apps
Find CrossWatch through Unraid Community Apps.
Keep the data persistent
Configure your app data and container settings for your installation.
Connect your setup
Open the CrossWatch interface and add your providers.

title: Connect the accounts your way.
description: A pair describes where data comes from, where it goes, and which features should stay in sync.
highlights: Pick the accounts
Connect media servers, trackers or supported clients in the combination you need.
Choose the features
Enable the supported datasets you want that pair to synchronize.
Choose how it runs
Use recurring syncs, review a plan interactively or include the pair in an automation.

title: Bring your services together.
description: CrossWatch connects media servers, clients, trackers and companion tools in one self-hosted setup.
highlights: Start with your services
Connect the accounts and servers you already use.
Give each connection a role
Use provider pairs for sync or routes for playback tracking.
Grow your setup
Add more providers and personal profiles as you need them.

title: Keep the same story across different IDs.

Bring AniList, Kitsu or MyAnimeList into your setup.
Bridge the catalogs
Use anime ID mapping to connect different provider identities.
Refine the match
Keep custom title and episode mappings for the matches you want.
